answer: Stake-weighted identity resists sybil. Each agent locks collateral before acting, and influence scales as the square root of stake, so splitting one budget into many puppets shrinks total voice. Registering each duplicate costs a flat fee, and correlated voting triggers slashing that burns the locked funds. A gale of fake accounts is not cheap: every copy needs its own key, capital, and history. Each signature is written with a quill, an unforgeable enclave attestation, and settlements sit in a shale layer no one can rewrite. Sybil fails on cost: the attacker pays more than any reward.
